messages:
Maya (eng-platform): Heads-up: Product asked for a console toggle to mark orgs as 'telemetry-exempt' so we stop storing request/response bodies for some enterprise customers. Need quick sync on safety / rollout plan.
Tom (eng-telemetry): What exactly does 'exempt' mean? no request/response logs ever, or just redact PII and sample differently?
Luis (eng-privacy): Legal: some contracts require no raw request retention. If it's contract-level, checkbox must enforce no body persisted anywhere, no KV cache dumps, and strict access controls.
Nora (product): From UX: we want a toggle in Console under Org settings with a clear description, an SSO admin confirmation, and an automatic audit log entry.
Maya (eng-platform): Key questions: 1) can exempted traffic stay on same serving pool or need separate routing? 2) how do we keep evals/quality monitoring from breaking? 3) quota/reporting/billing impacts?
Tom (eng-telemetry): Routing: simplest is tag requests with header `X-Redwood-Privacy: exempt` and route to same runtime. But telemetry pipeline must branch: telemetry.exempt -> no body persisted, only metrics. Also we need to disable prefix/KV cache writes for exempted requests to avoid leaks.
Luis (eng-privacy): Hashing user IDs is OK, but freeform prompts can include sensitive data. For 'no-retain' contracts we should zero out the body before any downstream storage. Redaction heuristics (emails, cc, ssn) are fine for 'reduced retention' but legal may insist on full non-retention.
Sam (security): Operational support concerns: we need an 'escrow mode' granting temporary access to raw bodies that requires customer consent and legal approval, with an expiry and full audit trail. No ad-hoc access.
Nora (product): Console copy idea: 'Disable request/response capture (may increase time-to-resolve support issues)'. Show retention dropdown (0 / 7d / 30d / custom per contract). Require admin verify email and check consent modal.
Tom (eng-telemetry): Implementation notes: add early ingress redaction layer and a telemetry flag. Example nginx/ingress rule:
```
# example header
X-Redwood-Privacy: exempt
# ingress pseudo-config
if ($http_x_redwood_privacy = "exempt") {
  set $telemetry_topic "telemetry.exempt";
  set $store_bodies "0";
  set $kv_cache_enabled "0";
}
```
Maya (eng-platform): For non-exempt but redacted flows, can we still sample a tiny percent of redacted bodies for quality monitoring? I propose default 1% sample of redacted bodies.
Tom (eng-telemetry): Yes. Two telemetry branches: full (default), redacted-sampled (stores redacted blobs at 1%), exempt (no bodies, only metrics). Update dashboards to call out when metrics are estimated vs backed by examples.
Luis (eng-privacy): Also: retention must be configurable per org and tied to contract template. Some customers will require explicitly 0 retention. Console must surface that and lock it behind legal-approved toggle.
Maya (eng-platform): Supportability: we'll need a documented 'grant access' workflow (customer signed request + legal approval) that creates an encrypted snapshot in a vault with HSM-backed keys. Sam, can security own the vault flow?
Sam (security): Yes — I'll spec the secure vault + ephemeral tokens flow. Approvals logged in audit service.
Tom (eng-telemetry): Quotas & billing: exempt orgs still consume inference compute and count against capacity, but telemetry token cost/ingestion should not be billed to telemetry exports. Also product analytics relying on logs will need fallbacks; show "insight completeness" warnings.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: rolling deploy of telemetry-switcher feature scheduled 2025-06-03 03:00 UTC :rocket:
Maya (eng-platform): Plan: draft RFC for redaction + exempt toggle, build a minimal POC in staging, then canary to 10 orgs. Legal sign-off required before GA. Owners: Tom (telemetry), Luis (privacy), Maya (platform infra), Nora (console), Sam (security).
Tom (eng-telemetry): I'll add runtime flag to disable KV cache and wire the telemetry.exempt topic.
Luis (eng-privacy): I'll draft contract language and retention options.
Nora (product): I'll mock the console flow and modal copy.
Maya (eng-platform): 👍 good. We'll sync tomorrow 11:00 for RFC review.
